cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Handedness – the preference for using one hand more than the other.

p.em: Example: Most people show right-handedness when writing or eating.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bipedalism – the ability to walk on two legs.

p.em: Example: Scientists believe bipedalism changed the way humans used their hands.

cosy-blockquote.p: Evolutionary milestone – an important stage in the development of a species.

p.em: Example: Learning to walk upright was a major evolutionary milestone.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bias – a tendency or preference toward something.

p.em: Example: Humans have a strong right-hand bias compared to other primates.

cosy-blockquote.p: Locomotion – movement from one place to another.

p.em: Example: Walking is the main form of human locomotion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Asymmetric – not equal or balanced on both sides.

p.em: Example: Researchers think humans developed more asymmetric hand use over time.
Example: Some hominins may have used tools with one hand more often than the other.
Example: Right-handedness is one of humanity’s most common traits.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dominance – stronger control, influence, or preference.

p.em: Example: The dominance of the right hand is unusual among animals.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reinforce – to make something stronger or more common.

p.em: Example: Culture may reinforce right-handed behavior in schools and daily life.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article's statistical logs, why is a persistent 9:1 ratio of right-to-left handedness stable across all human cultures?
★ Are you right-handed, left-handed, or ambidextrous?

What empirical evidence proves that early bipedalism changed the motor coordination loads on our upper limbs?
★ What is one daily task you find impossible to do with your non-dominant hand?

According to researchers, why is left-hemisphere speech localization considered a major evolutionary milestone for humans?
★ Do you have any left-handed friends or family members? Have they ever complained about right-handed tools?

How did the study measure right-hand bias during prehistoric tool excavation trials?
★ Have you ever tried to write or paint with your left hand for an afternoon?

What structural differences in bipedal locomotion distinguish human motor lateralization from other chimpanzees?
★ Do you feel that your physical coordination is better on one side of your body?

According to researchers, what makes the highly asymmetric layout of the human brain unique compared to other primates?
★ Were you ever encouraged or forced to use your right hand when you were a child?

What archaeological findings prove that early hominin species used asymmetric strokes when sharpening stone hand-axes?
★ Do you notice any strong habitual routines that you always start with a specific side?

Based on cognitive testing, why is hand preference considered an unbreakable biological trait rather than a cultural choice?
★ Do you consider yourself more logical, more creative, or a balance of both?

How does the study explain right-hemisphere dominance for spatial tasks in left-handed subjects?
★ What physical task (like playing an instrument or typing) required the most hand coordination to learn?

How does modern cultural bias reinforce right-handedness during preschool handwriting development?
★ Do you think biological differences are what make human skills so diverse?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research proves that natural handedness can be completely swapped using simple genetic regulators, will schools ban natural hand dominance in favor of ambidexterity?
★ Would losing small human differences make society more efficient or more boring?

As our understanding of bipedalism changes under low-gravity space colonies, future space-born humans will develop symmetrically coordinated feet instead of hands.
★ Do you think biology strongly influences a person's talents and ultimate career path?

Imagine future research proves that reaching an evolutionary milestone is directly predictable; will companies use brain scans to hire workers for specific manual tasks?
★ Where should society draw the ethical line when it comes to selecting a child's traits before birth?

If we discover how to eliminate right-hand bias entirely using brain-chips, will humans communicate twice as fast through symmetrical dual-keyboard typing?
★ Do you already notice changes in your attention span or physical habits due to screen use?

As spatial locomotion in virtual worlds becomes standard, our hands will decline in mass, resulting in symmetrical, highly simplified digits.
★ Would separating students based on their brain types help them succeed or create unfair labels?

Imagine future research shows that an asymmetric brain structure is three times more creative; will future parents genetically edit their children's brains to maximize asymmetry?
★ Would knowing a person's neurological profile change how you judge their character?

If we can sequence early hominin cognitive patterns, scientists will recreate ancient tools to test original neural pathways.
★ How physically different do you think humans living on other planets could become over time?

As pediatric technologies mature, a child's hand trait will be calibrated dynamically using non-invasive electronic gloves.
★ Do you think becoming physically 'perfect' would actually improve your happiness?

Imagine future research proves that right-hand dominance is a byproduct of obsolete language pathways; will we completely drop hand preferences when communicating using telepathy?
★ Why do you think humans feel more comfortable with imperfect, human-like behavior in machines?

As neural monitors are integrated, we will automatically reinforce bilateral motor coordination during early childhood development.
★ Do you think modern digital multitasking is improving or weakening our overall focus?

ul.li: Incorrect: The most of humans → Correct: Most humans ((Generalization))
Incorrect: It depends of your brain → Correct: It depends on your brain ((Depends on))
Incorrect: I am using my right hand since always → Correct: I have always used my right hand ((Present Perfect))
Incorrect: I can't to write with my left hand → Correct: I can't write with my left hand ((Modal verb + infinitive))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
